title: Composition, inheritance, and method resolution
sources: Python documentation: super and method resolution order
masterChecklist: Inheritance, composition, mixins, multiple inheritance, MRO, super and polymorphism
Classes, instances, methods, self, constructors, attributes, class versus instance variables
Design trade-offs, cohesion/coupling, substitution and maintainable object boundaries
whyItMatters: Inheritance can reuse behavior, but it also creates a strong relationship between parent and child. Composition—giving an object a collaborator—often keeps designs smaller, easier to test, and easier to change.
simpleExplanation: Inheritance models an is-a relationship: a TimedReview can be a kind of Review. Composition models a has-a relationship: a Review has a notifier. super() follows Python's method resolution order so cooperating classes can call the next implementation rather than naming a specific parent directly.
mentalModel: Inheritance is a family recipe that each child recipe extends. Composition is a meal assembled from separate ingredients. A family recipe can be useful, but adding too many inherited rules makes it hard to know which recipe step runs next.
outcomes: Distinguish is-a from has-a design relationships.
Use composition for a replaceable collaborator.
Explain why super() is safer than hard-coding a parent in cooperative inheritance.
Recognize when multiple inheritance adds more complexity than value.

realWorldExample.scenario: A study review can send a reminder through different delivery methods without changing its core scheduling rule.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Making EmailReview, SmsReview, DesktopReview, and every combination through inheritance can produce a class explosion and confusing method order.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Keep Review responsible for the review rule and inject a notifier object that provides send(message). Choose inheritance only when the subtype truly honors the same public contract.

explanation: ConsoleNotifier has one focused responsibility: send a message.
Review receives a notifier instead of inheriting every delivery behavior.
remind keeps the domain rule and delegates delivery through the collaborator.
A test can supply a simple fake notifier without changing Review.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Create a second notifier class that returns a different prefix. Review can use it without being rewritten.

procedure: Name the responsibilities that may change independently.
Prefer composition when one object needs another service or strategy.
Use inheritance only when a child can safely stand in for its parent contract.
Keep mixins narrow and document their required methods/state.
Use super() in cooperative inheritance and test the method-resolution behavior explicitly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using inheritance only to reuse a few lines of code.
commonMistakes.why: It couples unrelated concepts and creates fragile hierarchy behavior.
commonMistakes.avoid: Extract a helper or compose a collaborator when the relationship is has-a.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling a specific parent method instead of super() in a cooperative hierarchy.
commonMistakes.why: It can skip another class in the method resolution order.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use super() when classes are designed to cooperate through MRO.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a mixin that silently requires undocumented attributes.
commonMistakes.why: A class can fail far from the source of the missing requirement.
commonMistakes.avoid: Keep mixin contracts explicit, small, and tested.

lab.title: Send a fictional review through a composed notifier
lab.safety: Uses only local return strings; no message is sent externally.
guidedSteps: Write Review.__init__ accepting title and notifier.
Write remind to call notifier.send with a review message.
checks: Review does not inherit from ConsoleNotifier.
Does not contact any external service.
lab.solutionExplanation: Review owns the review behavior and delegates only the replaceable delivery behavior to its notifier. This keeps each class small and lets tests substitute a controlled notifier.
challenges: Find the bug: make Review inherit from ConsoleNotifier even though it is not itself a notifier.
Experiment: add a FakeNotifier that stores messages in a list for a test.
lab.testCode:
review = Review('Functions', ConsoleNotifier())
assert review.remind() == 'notice: Review Functions'
class CaptureNotifier:
    def send(self, message):
        return f'captured: {message}'
assert Review('Loops', CaptureNotifier()).remind() == 'captured: Review Loops'
print('PASS: notifier composition')

projectConnection.milestone: Separate scheduling logic from delivery logic and test the scheduler with a fake notifier.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: A new delivery method can be introduced without changing the review scheduling rule or creating a new inheritance combination.

assessment.question: When is composition often preferable?
assessment.answer: When an object needs a replaceable collaborator or service—a has-a relationship.

assessment.question: What relationship does inheritance model best?
assessment.answer: A true is-a relationship where the child honors the parent contract.
assessment.explanation: Reuse alone is not enough reason for inheritance.

assessment.question: Why use super in cooperative inheritance?
assessment.answer: It follows the method resolution order and lets other cooperating classes participate.
assessment.explanation: Hard-coded parent calls can skip behavior unexpectedly.
